blocks.label: Exact finite counting identities
blocks.text: These identities follow from coefficient extraction. They do not establish a positive Goldbach count at every even integer or infinitely many twin primes.
Keep the counting convention explicit: unequal pairs appear twice in the ordered count, while a repeated-prime diagonal appears once. Laurent exponents encode the translation q − p = 2.

blocks.label: Finding of the written-proof review
blocks.text: These are correct, elementary generating-function encodings of the counting definitions. They establish neither positivity of G(N) for every even N ≥ 4 nor infinitely many twin primes.

Their usefulness is organizational: one polynomial product expresses reflection and another expresses translation. Any proposed lower bound or asymptotic statement must add a separate argument. The reviewed source states these limits explicitly [S2].
